title: Docker: image, container, process, and volume
outcome: Reconstruct what survives stop, restart, replacement, and image rebuild.
useCase: Remembering Docker by lifecycle instead of command memorization.
drawbacks: State, platform, access, and recovery still need explicit design.
version: Pinned local examples · version-labelled configuration fragments
cue: Image is the recipe. Container is the instance. Volume is a data decision.

trace.title: Image artifact
trace.detail: An image is a packaged filesystem/configuration template. A container is a running or stopped instance with its own writable layer. It runs processes using the host kernel’s container facilities; it is not automatically a whole independent virtual machine.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Build image → create container → start main process → write to layer/volume → stop → restart or replace. Before each step, predict which bytes and process state remain.

Trace a Rails upload written locally. A replacement container starts from the image again; it does not inherit the old writable layer. External object storage solves a different boundary from packaging.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: EXPOSE documents a container port; it does not publish it to the host. A running container can contain a failing app. A volume is not itself a tested backup.
